priorPublicContract.question: Switch to scheduling. Implement Python best_schedule(jobs,K), where each job has integer start, end, and signed profit; start is less than end, and intervals are half-open. Input indices are job ids. There are at most 2,000 jobs, K is between zero and 50, and absolute profits are at most one trillion. Return optimal profit and selected ids, or None if impossible. Define predecessor-search boundaries and DP states, reconstruct without selecting a job twice, and prove O(nK+n log n) time. Test touching intervals, negative profits, K zero, and infeasibility. Crucially, select exactly K jobs, not at most K: explain why zero-initializing every DP state fails.

Change the scheduling contract: job i has a nonnegative integer cleanup delay g[i]. If selected job j follows i, require end[i] + g[i] <= start[j]; no cleanup deadline applies after the final job. Keep exactly K and the same complexity bound. Your expression `bisect_right(ends, job[1], 0, i)` no longer captures compatibility. Give a minimal failing trace for your old code, then executable patched Python. Can compatible predecessors still form a prefix under some ordering? Prove your ordering and reconstruction remain valid, including equal completion times and negative profits.

manualSourceReview.ordering: Compatibility requires c_i=end_i+g_i <= start_j < end_j <= c_j, so any compatible predecessor has strictly smaller completion. Equal-completion jobs cannot follow one another.
manualSourceReview.predecessorBoundary: bisect_right searches only the earlier prefix and includes completions equal to the new start. The resulting prefix index is strictly before the current job, preventing its reuse.
manualSourceReview.exactlyK: Only the zero-count row is initialized to zero. Positive-count infeasible states remain None; negative optima remain eligible. Each take consumes one count and jumps to its compatible predecessor prefix.
manualSourceReview.finalCleanup: There is no external completion deadline on the final selected job. A huge cleanup value changes ordering but does not prevent selection as the last job.
manualSourceReview.workBound: Sorting and predecessor searches use O(N log N) arithmetic comparisons; DP uses O(NK) transitions and O(N(K+1)) storage. The answer explicitly notes that arbitrary-precision timestamp/cleanup bit lengths add integer-operation costs.
